findings.reason: The protected Python solution determines if s and t are one edit distance apart by enforcing len(t) >= len(s), scanning character pointers first and second, and tracking edit count. When a mismatch is encountered, it increments edits and advances either both pointers (for equal lengths) or second only (for insertion). The algorithm runs in O(m + n) time and O(1) space; no candidate is required.
Restricting length difference to at most 1 and advancing pointers according to equal length (replacement) versus unequal length (insertion) accurately detects exactly one edit distance.
Pointers inspect each string character at most once, yielding O(m + n) time. Auxiliary space is O(1) for scalar pointer and count variables. Complexity evidence is inherited and hash-bound.
Accepts strings s and t, returning a boolean indicating if they are exactly one edit distance apart.

The approach accurately details length difference normalization, single-pass dual-pointer traversal, edit classification (replacement vs insertion), and O(m + n) time / O(1) space bounds. Alternatives and edge cases cover full DP edit distance overheads, all-one-edit generation costs, suffix slicing memory overheads, dual empty strings zero-edit rejection, empty vs single-character insertion cases, case sensitivity rules, and trailing character count logic.
